To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

As a life-long New York City resident, I am concerned about the Axon-branded Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) cameras sprouting up around the city. While security is important, recent news stories (generally around Flock, a competitor to Axon) has shown that abuse of these systems is trivial and largely tolerated.

In the interest of community control of our own police force, I am requesting the following information:
- Location of all Axon cameras with ALPR functionality (whether fixed or mobile)
- Date of activation
- Activity Reports from these cameras including when they were queried and for what reason. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as actual license plate tags can be redacted or omitted. Officer names should be anonymized, but not omitted, so potential bad behavior can be identified and relayed to the NYPD.

Thanks in advance for your cooperation under NY's FOIL.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Peter Gravelle

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I am requesting access to and copies of records held by the National Archives and Records Administration that were identified by the Federal Bureau of Investigation as responsive to my FOIPA request but transferred to NARA custody rather than processed directly by the FBI.

By letter dated September 18, 2026 (FOIPA Request No. 1755138-000, Subject: "Revolutionary War Organization"), the FBI's Record/Information Dissemination Section advised that records potentially responsive to my request were transferred to NARA, and directed me to reference the following FBI file numbers, all bearing FBI Classification 100 (Domestic Security), found within Record Group 65, Records of the Federal Bureau of Investigation:

● 100-HQ-452863
● 100-HQ-473049
● 100-HQ-442715
● 100-HQ-442786
● 100-HQ-6877

● 100-HQ-17319
● 100-HQ-272700
● 100-NY-148047-3070
● 100-NY-161514
● 100-NY-167072
● 100-HQ-455011

A copy of the document can be found online here: 
https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2026/09/21/E13d990ba39b6e32a28bbd3f319338954c77ac165da427a85d9_Q341556_D165960914.pdf

I ask that NARA search the Classification 100 (Domestic Security) Headquarters Case Files series for the "HQ" numbers listed above, and the corresponding New York Field Office Case Files series for the "NY" numbers, and provide copies of all file units associated with each number. If any of these numbers (particularly 100-HQ-3-65, given its unusually low base file number) correspond to a general or umbrella file to which sub-files or cross-references relating
to the "Revolutionary War Organization" (also referenced in some records as "Revolutionary War Organizations") were later appended, I request that NARA identify the specific sub-file(s) or serials pertaining to that organization and process those portions.

If any portion of this request is denied, please provide a description of each withheld record, the specific exemption(s) claimed, and segregate and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.
